grand_strategy.reading: Burkina Faso's grand strategy is sovereignty by rupture: it has left ECOWAS and France, built a confederation with Mali and Niger, and taken Russian instructors to guard the regime while the state takes over the gold mines to pay for the war. The ruptures buy autonomy at the cost of the channels that once held its security and its capital, and the mine takeover frightens the investors that the mines need. The war against JNIM is the test that the sovereignty doctrine has not yet passed, and this card rests on 2024 to mid-2026 sources without verified 2026 battlefield data, so the transition timetable and the 2025 US aid cut are not confirmed here.

stances.note: The Alliance of Sahel States is the bloc Burkina chose after leaving ECOWAS: a pact signed in July 2024 with Mali and Niger (Al Jazeera headline; the exit from ECOWAS is dated January 2024, DW). The grade ally rests on the pact; the treaty text was not opened here, so whether it carries a defence clause is not verified. Bond affinity is our reading: the three juntas share a coup origin, the sovereignty frame and a hostility to ECOWAS and France, with no kinship. Two tier 3 sources only, so C. The MLI card reads the same pact as ally from its side.

stances.note: Burkina broke off diplomatic relations with France on 26 June 2026, through its communications minister, citing non-interference and accusing France of supporting 'subversive networks' and 'terrorists'. Paris called the move hostile and unfounded and is weighing reciprocal measures. The French foreign ministry's own statement was seen in search results but not opened; the Reuters copy was read. Rival, not adversary: both sides keep the break at state level and the junta says the people's ties stand. Bond grievance is our reading: the colonial past and the 2023 expulsion of French forces. The 2023 expulsion and the media bans are not sourced in this pass; the cooling since January 2023 rests on Wikipedia's citation of Reuters, not opened.

stances.note: Adversary is our reading, and no source uses the word. The structure is mortal: JNIM fights to take the state's territory and the junta fights to destroy the group, so each side's aim is the other's defeat. The Barsalogho attack (August 2024) is the dated marker; the start of the war is not dated here. Mirror: the BEN card's ACLED source says JNIM uses Tapoa and Kompienga provinces in Burkina Faso for raids into Benin; that is about the group's use of Burkinabe ground, not an act of the state. Bond grievance is our reading of an open war with massacres on both sides. Gaps: the Djibo attack is not verified (the search found only Barsalogho); the junta's own casualty figures are not published here.

stances_toward.note: Cooperation out of necessity under strain. Reluctant partner is our reading (C): relations soured after the 2022 coup and the December 2022 summons, yet security cooperation tightened after the 14 February 2026 Titao attack that killed Ghanaian traders (AFP). The necessity is the JNIM spillover across a porous northern border. The resisting-alignment half is not sourced here. Trend warming is our reading: seven instruments signed in February 2026 and boundary talks in June 2026, against the strain of 2022-25. Bond none: the index notes Sankara-era closeness, which is historical; no current kinship or grievance is documented. Sources are press and advocacy analysis, not official statements.

relations_to.summary: JNIM attacks in northern Benin rose sharply in 2025: an 8 January assault on the Point Triple base killed at least 28 soldiers and an attack on 17 April killed at least 54 (government toll, as reported). ACLED says JNIM uses Tapoa and Kompienga provinces in Burkina Faso as staging grounds for incursions into Benin. The Burkina state is not named as responsible; this row records the spillover, not a Burkinabe act.
relations_to.note: Counts differ by source (ADF Magazine reports 30 soldiers for January, ACLED 34). The 17 April toll is from a summary of the government's announcement, not opened.
